onboarding.description: Supercharge your workflow on Google AI Studio, Gemini, ChatGPT, and Claude with a better way to organize your chats and a beautiful UI.
onboarding.openSourceNote: Free & open-source, built and maintained by a solo developer. Thank you for your support!
onboarding.loginRequired: Please log in to the AI platform first — the sidebar activates on the platform page after you sign in.

onboarding.headline: Less clutter.
onboarding.intro: A calmer home for your Gemini and AI Studio conversations. Organize what matters, find it faster, and keep your best prompts close.

onboarding.tutorialTitle: A little tour. A head start.

onboarding.videoNote: The tutorial opens in a new YouTube tab, since extension pages can't host the player.
onboarding.footerNote: Made for a more thoughtful workflow.

welcome.title: Welcome to Better Sidebar. Here's a small gift to start with
welcome.intro: Better Sidebar helps you keep your Gemini and AI Studio chats in order: folders, tags, full-text search, a prompt library, and export. All of that is free, and it stays free.
welcome.powerPack: On top of it there's Power Pack, an optional add-on that turns the built-in AI agents from helpers that look things up into helpers that actually get things done. Since you're new here, it's unlocked for your first 3 days, so you can see whether it fits your workflow before deciding anything.
welcome.sidebarAgentDesc: Describe it in a sentence, and it creates folders, sorts your chats, and batch-tags or renames across your whole history.
welcome.workspaceAgentDesc: More workspaces and more files, for analyzing or editing your Word, Excel, PDF and code files.
welcome.browserAgentDesc: Goes beyond suggestions to actually group your tabs, close duplicates and tidy up bookmark folders, with a snapshot you can roll back.
welcome.webAgentDesc: Hand it a web page and it fills in forms, clicks through steps or pulls tables together, and you approve every action.
welcome.exportDesc: Send conversations and snippets straight to your notes.
welcome.reassurance: No card needed and nothing to cancel. When the trial ends, you simply go back to the free version, and everything you've organized stays where it is.

classify.label: Organize history
classify.text: Organize my unfiled chats: group them by topic and show me the plan first. If current folders don't fit, create new ones and move the chats there. Finally, tag each chat based on its content, reusing my existing tags to avoid duplicates.

search.label: Deep search
search.text: Find all mentions of 'Docker deployment'. Search thoroughly across chats, message bodies, and code snippets, not just titles. Order them from newest to oldest, providing a one-line summary for each and indicating which folder it's in.

export.label: Batch export & archive
export.text: Export all chats in my 'Work' folder from March onwards to Markdown format, one file per chat, and pack them in a zip. If any chat doesn't have its messages synced yet, let me know before exporting.

prompts.label: Refactor prompt library
prompts.text: Clean up my prompt library: rename the ones that are hard to find via / by putting the keyword at the beginning. Extract the repeated 'role + output format' block into a shared prompt and import it into the others. If a variable only has a few fixed options, change it to a dropdown menu.

snippets.label: Clean up snippets
snippets.text: My snippet inbox is a mess. Group them into folders by topic, and shorten titles that are still my original question into a brief summary. If the same content is saved twice, keep only the oldest one. Show me the list before deleting anything.

browserIntro.title: Let AI tidy up your tabs and bookmarks
browserIntro.howToUseContent:
Browser Agent works on your Chrome windows: open tabs, tab groups and bookmarks. It sees titles and addresses, not page contents.

How to use:
Type >Browser Agent in the chat input, then describe what you want organized — for example "group these tabs by topic and collapse the ones I am not using" or "bookmark this window and organize loose bookmarks into folders".

What it can do:
- Tabs: open new tabs, switch, reorder, move between windows, pin.
- Tab groups: create, rename, recolor, collapse, dissolve.
- Bookmarks: save pages as bookmarks, create folders, rename, and move things between folders.
- Closing tabs and deleting bookmarks are sensitive operations, off unless you turn them on in settings.

Safe and reversible:
- Preview before applying: Reading needs no confirmation. Any modification presents a clear preview first, and applies only after you approve it.
- Undo anytime: All changes are recorded locally and can be restored from the panel at any time.

💡 Tip: "Organize my tabs" never means closing them. If you want things removed, say so explicitly — otherwise it will gather them into a group or folder and leave the decision to you.

stash.text: I want this window down to the handful I am actually working in. Bookmark everything else into a new folder named for today, keep the pinned tabs and anything from my company domain open, then show me the list before you close a single tab.

bookmarks.label: Sort the bookmarks
bookmarks.text: Go through my bookmarks bar. Group the loose ones into folders by topic and move them in, rename the ones whose title is still the page title into something I would recognise, and tell me which ones look like duplicates instead of deleting them.

open.label: Set up a workspace
open.text: Open the tabs I need for a review session: our repo, the issue tracker and the design doc. Put them in one group called Review, pin the repo, and leave everything I already have open where it is.

prune.label: Clear out the dead ends
prune.text: Show me the bookmarks that look stale — untitled ones, search result pages, anything saved twice. List them with the folder each one is in, and let me pick which to delete rather than deciding for me.

dedupe.label: Close the duplicates
dedupe.text: I have the same pages open multiple times. Close the duplicates and keep one of each — the pinned or grouped copy if there is one, otherwise the oldest. Two addresses only count as the same page if the full URL matches. Do the same for my bookmarks if the same link is saved in more than one folder.

workspaceIntro.title: Collaborate with AI on your Workspace documents
workspaceIntro.body: Files here persist across chats and are shared between Gemini and AI Studio. Type > Workspace in the chat input to put this agent to work on them.
workspaceIntro.detail: Text files are read and edited directly. Word documents are read by outline and section. It cannot see your conversations or anything outside this workspace, and every change is confirmed before it runs.
workspaceIntro.howToUseContent:
Workspace is your dedicated file environment where AI can directly read, write, edit, and create documents and code from scratch.

How to use:
Type >Workspace in the chat input to activate the agent. You can drag and drop existing files into the workspace, or simply ask the AI to generate new files from scratch (e.g. building a frontend project from the ground up).

Supported Formats & Capabilities:
- Plain Text & Code (.html, .js, .ts, .py, .md, .txt, etc.): Full support for creation from scratch and precise editing! Ask AI to scaffold an entire frontend project, write scripts, draft Markdown notes, or refactor existing code.
- Word (.docx): Review papers chapter by chapter, rewrite paragraphs with tracked changes, and add reviewer comments (requires uploading existing files).
- Excel (.xlsx/.csv): Analyze data, write formulas, and add columns without altering original formats or charts (requires uploading existing files).
- PDF: Read papers and reports, extract text, merge pages, and add annotations.
- PowerPoint (.pptx): Read and edit slide content and speaker notes.
- Subtitles (.srt/.vtt): Translate and polish subtitles while preserving timestamps.

💡 Tip: Text and code files can be created from scratch and freely edited. Special formats (Word, Excel, PPT, PDF) currently focus on reading, annotating, and precisely editing existing files while preserving their original formatting.

consent.title: Before you use the Web Agent
consent.intro: The Web Agent lets the AI read web pages and operate them for you: clicking, typing and running scripts in your browser. Please read this before turning it on.

actsAsYou.title: It acts as you
actsAsYou.body: The agent works in your own browser, with your logged-in accounts. Whatever it does — submitting a form, sending a message, placing an order — is done under your name, and may not be reversible.

dataToAi.title: Page content goes to the AI
dataToAi.body: Everything the agent reads from a page (text, links, form values) becomes part of your Gemini conversation and is sent to Google. Password fields are never read.

injection.title: Web pages can try to trick it
injection.body: A page can contain hidden instructions written for an AI ("prompt injection"). Check every action before you approve it, especially on sites you do not know.

sensitive.title: Keep it away from sensitive pages
sensitive.body: Do not use it on banking, payment, medical or account-security pages, or anywhere a mistake would be expensive.

mistakes.title: The AI makes mistakes
mistakes.body: It can click the wrong thing or misread a page. You approve every click, every piece of typing and every script. Stay at the computer while it runs.

stop.title: How to stop it
stop.body: Chrome shows a "started debugging this browser" bar on every page the agent controls. Press Cancel on that bar, or close the side panel, and it stops immediately.

responsibility.title: You are responsible for what you approve
responsibility.body: Including following the terms of the websites you use it on. Better Sidebar is provided as is, and is not liable for losses caused by actions you approved.

consent.permissionNote: The agent operates pages through Chrome's page debugger. While it works, Chrome shows a debugging bar on those pages.
consent.checkbox: I have read and understand these risks
